weave.text: Every love story has an opening scene, and theirs was not the stuff of films. {met}. Neither of them knew it yet. That ordinary moment was quietly rearranging the rest of their lives.
Ask what came first and the answer arrives without a pause. {s_first}. Some things you notice once. Some things you keep noticing for the rest of your life.

{years} years later, the details have only grown sweeter. There are a thousand cups of tea in there, a few slammed doors, far more apologies than anyone counted, and a love that got stronger every time it was tested.
If you want to know how love actually looks after all this time, it looks like this: {love|low}. Small enough to miss. Big enough to build a life on.
Then there is {joke}. Do not ask. You will not get a straight answer, only two people trying very hard not to laugh.
The memory they go back to most is this one. {trip}. Not because it was perfect, but because they were together for every second of it.
Their idea of a perfect day is beautifully simple. {s_ordinary}. Nothing to prove, nowhere to be, nobody else they would rather be with.
And every week, without fail, there is {s_tradition|low}. Some traditions are passed down. The best ones you make up together.

weave.text: Long before the flowers and the seating plan, there was this. {met}. It is the kind of beginning that only makes sense looking back, and now it makes all the sense in the world.
{from} knew before they did, of course. {s_knew}. Some people simply fit, and the rest of us just watch it happen.
What they have is hard to put into words, so {from} tried anyway: {secret|low}. Every couple has a secret recipe. Theirs is the sweetest one going.
When the music starts it will be {song|low}, and for three minutes the whole room will go very quiet and very soft.
Ask anyone who was there about the day and you will hear the same thing first. {s_best}. Weddings are made of moments like that.
As for married life, {from} has one piece of advice, and it is a good one. {s_advice}.
Three words for the two of them, said with a full heart: {words|low}. That is how they will be remembered, and how they will go on.

weave.text: In {married} two young people stood side by side and promised each other forever. They had no idea what forever would ask of them. They said yes anyway, and then they kept saying it, every single day.
It began like this: {met|low}. A small, funny start to something enormous.
Look at what they built. {s_built}. Every one of those people exists because two people chose each other and did not let go.
Ask them the secret and they will laugh, then say it as though it is obvious. {secret}. Perhaps it is. Perhaps the hard part is doing it for {years} years.
And there is always one story that gets told. {moment}. Every family has its legends. This one is theirs.
The grandchildren will tell you the real lesson. {s_learned}. Nobody had to teach it. They just watched.
